name: Inca Empire

areaKm2.note: Infobox ~2,000,000 km2 (high); Seshat codes 0.5-2.0 million km2 for 1375-1532 (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/83). The world_1530 polygon measures ~1.17 million km2 (low) and misses much of Chile and northwest Argentina.

population.note: Estimates range from 4 to 37 million; most fall between 6 and 14 million (the article); 10 million is McEwan's mid-range figure. Seshat codes 6-14 million for 1532 (https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/83). Smallpox reached the Andes c. 1525-28, before this snapshot.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Cusco 20,000-100,000 (Seshat), administrative centres (Huanuco Pampa, Tumebamba); mostly rural ayllus.

activePersonnel.note: Wartime snapshot during the civil war (1529-32): Atahualpa's veteran northern army numbered 50,000-100,000 initially, later 250,000 (via the article); Huascar fielded large levies. Counted here: the noble guard (10,000, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_army), officers, frontier garrisons and the veteran field armies of Quizquiz and Chalcuchimac.

trainedReserves.note: Commoners (hatun runa) owed military mit'a; Inca and Spanish accounts say the empire could field armies of 100,000 at a time and 200,000 in a single army under Huayna Capac (via the article).

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Officers' staff, quipucamayocs, depot (qullqa) and tambo personnel attached to armies.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Decimal census organisation let the state draft men aged 25-50 by rotation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_army).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Macemen and spearmen (bronze-headed star maces, halberds) of the field armies.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25 minus: bronze and stone weapons, quilted armour, against steel and gunpowder.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: veterans of Huayna Capac's northern wars.

count.note: Educated guess. Slingers, bola throwers and Antisuyu archers.
Educated guess. Scouts and auxiliary skirmishers.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: decimal command hierarchy, able generals (Quizquiz, Chalcuchimac, Rumi Nawi).

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: civil war split the empire; ethnic squads, Canari and Chachapoya hostility.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5: victorious northern army confident, southern levies demoralised.

weapons.note: Anchor 1-2: arsenical bronze maces and axes, slings, bolas, bows; no iron. No horses in the Americas before 1519 and no gunpowder; role absent.

armor.note: Anchor 1: quilted cotton tunics, wooden and cane helmets, shields.

ships.note: Anchor 0: balsa sailing rafts and reed boats.

fortification.note: Anchor 3 minus: megalithic ashlar walls (Sacsayhuaman) and pukara hillforts.

logistics.note: Anchor 3 minus: engineered road network with qullqa storehouse depots, but only llamas and porters to carry.

communications.note: Anchor 2-3: chasqui relay runners and quipu records.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 Peru 1595 = 880, 1600 = 921 (2011 int$, via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true), colonial with silver mining; pre-contact set lower.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Labour tax (mit'a) and state storehouses fed armies; high = civil war.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Cloth (cumbi), metalwork, state workshops.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Terraces, freeze-dried chuno and state granaries holding years of supply.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Qhapaq Nan about 40,000 km long in total (the article); low allows for unmaintained sections in 1530.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. No navy; balsa-raft trade at Tumbes.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Armies on the road network drew on qullqa every day's march; off the roads porters and llamas limited range.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Llama pack herds (about 30 kg each); no draught animals.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: high mountains and altitude, fortresses and depots; civil war undercuts population support.

notes: Snapshot = 1530, during the Inca civil war between Huascar and Atahualpa (1529-32), two years before Pizarro reached Cajamarca. Personnel convention: the noble guard, officers, garrisons and the veteran field armies under arms are activePersonnel; the mit'a levy is trainedReserves. Civil-war army sizes (Huascar ~400,000, Atahualpa 250,000) come from chronicles via the Inca Civil War article and are not used as mids. No horses, no iron, no gunpowder. Population is disputed (4-37 million; most 6-14 million). D'Altroy (The Incas) not consulted directly. Population convention: all four suyu, both factions.
